module.title: High-Order Partial Assembly and Matrix-Free Operators
module.expensive_path: For every operator action, restrict the global vector to element-local vectors, interpolate the nodal values and their gradients to quadrature points with a sequence of one-dimensional tensor contractions, apply the pointwise geometric and coefficient factors stored per quadrature point, contract back with the transposed basis, and assemble by gather-add. At polynomial order p in d dimensions this costs O(p^(d+1)) per element instead of the O(p^(2d)) of a stored element matrix, and it is the inner loop of every Krylov iteration in a high-order run, so it dominates wall time for orders above about two.
module.rationale: Partial assembly and matrix-free evaluation of scalar and vector H1 and L2 operators (mass, diffusion, elasticity, gradient and discrete interpolation) is one coherent tensor-contraction kernel family sharing a quadrature-interpolator and element-restriction layer. It is the path MFEM itself targets on accelerators, and it is distinct from the H(curl) and H(div) kernel family and from the face-integral family of discontinuous Galerkin.
excluded: H(curl) and H(div) kernels and their mixed forms are owned by hcurl-hdiv-electromagnetics.
Face-integral and discontinuous Galerkin kernels are owned by dg-hyperbolic-transport.
Nonlinear vector-convection kernels are owned by nonlinear-solvers-and-time-integration.
NURBS patch assembly is owned by nurbs-isogeometric.
The Krylov solvers and preconditioners that call these operators are owned by solvers-and-preconditioners.
hazards: Upstream ships no reference output for the examples; `make test` only checks exit codes, so each check's reference must be generated by the pinned CPU build and the graded quantity chosen from what the example actually writes (mesh and grid-function files) or prints (the final L2 error).
Conjugate-gradient iteration counts printed by the examples are adaptive bookkeeping and must never be graded.

Element and face storage order, and the byNODES versus byVDIM degree-of-freedom ordering, may legitimately differ; the graded comparison must key on the physical degree of freedom of a fixed mesh and space.
Fully assembled and partially assembled paths differ in floating-point summation order; test_fa_determinism.cpp exists upstream precisely because assembly order is not reproducible across backends.

Four of the module's unit test files (test_pa_coeff.cpp, test_pa_grad.cpp, test_pa_idinterp.cpp, test_coefficient.cpp) call mfem::Vector::Randomize() with no argument, which seeds libc srand() from time(0); a check built from one of them must pin the seed in its own initial condition, and the seeded stream is reproducible only within one C library.
